name: SlingPack_13x7x4
title: Sling Pack 13 × 7 × 4
description: Crossbody sling — a small tablet, a packed jacket, or a day's worth of everything. Wears across the chest or dropped onto the hip. The most comfortable size in the family to build: at 4" of depth the coil clears the binding flange by ⅜" and the webbing by 7/16", so nothing is marginal and 1" webbing fits without argument.

placements.label: 10" grab handle, bracketing the chassis overlap

hardware.note: opening is 12⅛"; shorten with a new bar-tacked stop
each on a 4" external tab, tacked through to the chassis

notes.title: This is the size with margin everywhere
notes.body: Depth is the constraint that bites first in this family — below about 2½" a webbing chassis stops fitting beside the zipper, and below about 1½" the gusset face gets too narrow to bind cleanly. At 4" nothing is close: ⅜" of visible shell outboard of the coil and a 7/16" gap to the webbing. If you are learning the construction, build this one first and the HipPack second.

notes.title: Two rings carry, two stabilise
notes.body: Rings 1 and 2 sit at the top of each side face and take the sling. Rings 3 and 4 on the base give a stabiliser strap something to pull against so the bag does not swing forward when you lean — the same geometry the tote uses for its backpack lower pair. Both stay rigged at once.

notes.title: Make a shoulder pad
notes.body: Interface-pressure research is unambiguous that wider straps are markedly more comfortable, with the best results around 8 cm, and 1" webbing is narrow for a single strap carrying the whole bag. A slip-on pad, or a Cordura sleeve over closed-cell foam, costs nothing structurally.

notes.title: The whole bag nests in a third of a yard
notes.body: Cordura comes 60" wide and every piece — both panels, the gusset cut long, both zip strips and the binding — shelf-nests into a strip well under 12" deep. Buy half a yard and the offcut covers a wear strip and a pocket.

open_questions.title: The sling strap is declared, not derived
open_questions.body: 56" of webbing, a tri-glide and two hooks are written down, but nothing computes them from the finished size or from a declared wearer. Change the bag and the strap figure will not move with it.

open_questions.title: No pockets
open_questions.body: A 13 × 7 × 4 bag with one cavity is a sack. At this size a divided back-panel pocket earns its place more than it does on the HipPack — the StadiumTote's full-width, no-bottom-seam pocket is the pattern to copy, and it costs one hand-declared piece plus its bound top edge.
